title: Health and Economic After-effects in Leicester Tuberculosis Cohort
official: Quantifying the Short to Long-term Physical, Psychological, and Socioeconomic Consequences of Pulmonary and Extra-pulmonary Tuberculosis in Patients in Leicester: a Longitudinal Cohort Study.
summary:
HEAL-TB (Health and Economic After-effects in Leicester Tuberculosis cohort) is a prospective observational study examining recovery among adults with pulmonary and extrapulmonary tuberculosis (TB). The study aims to understand how physical health, mental health, quality of life, daily activity, work and economic wellbeing change during TB treatment and up to 12 months after treatment completion.

Participants may join the study at different stages, from diagnosis until six months after completing TB treatment, and will be followed prospectively until 12 months after treatment completion. The study uses questionnaires, lung function testing, the Incremental Shuttle Walk Test, wrist-worn activity monitoring and information collected during routine clinical care. No experimental treatment is provided and participants continue to receive their usual NHS care.

The study aims to describe recovery over time, compare recovery following pulmonary and extrapulmonary TB, and identify factors associated with persistent health problems or poorer recovery.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Aged 16 years or above.
* Any sex/gender.
* Pulmonary or extrapulmonary tuberculosis, receiving or having recently completed tuberculosis treatment, with tuberculosis care or follow-up provided through University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust. The latest entry point into the cohort is six months after treatment completion.
* Willing and able to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Expected to move out of the area or unable to attend follow-up visits.
* Prisoners or people under custodial care.
* Currently involved in research or recently involved in other research.
